title: Pre-Analysis — Interim Sealing Standard for the Aft Lower Shell Longitudinal Joints
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of the first sealing and drainage standard for the aft lower shell joints, covering the general repair practice already applied at the joint land, the illustrated part list and the compartment content that has to be removed to reach the area.

sections.objective: Establish what the early-build fleet already carries at the aft lower shell longitudinal joints before a first sealing and drainage standard is fixed, and in particular whether the plug repairs already embodied under the general metallic repair practice can be left in place under the new sealant scheme. The work order was raised internally by the aft fuselage design office after moisture was found standing below the joint on three aircraft returned for a heavy check, and it was asked to report before the standard was frozen for the production line.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. The one that shaped the design was the general oversize hole and plug repair practice: a significant part of the early fleet has plugs at the joint land, and the sealant bead of the proposed standard would have been laid directly over them with no qualification behind it. The analysis could not show that the bead would hold on a plugged land, and the standard was therefore released with a condition requiring the plug population to be recorded and the bead to stop short of it. The remaining findings were content rather than design: the illustrated part list carries the old sealant and fastener call-out, the aft compartment wiring runs along the same sill and the cargo lining panels have to come out to reach the joint at all.
sections.next_steps: Record the plug population on the affected aircraft from the repair files before the first embodiment, and hand the qualification gap for a bead over a plugged land to the materials laboratory as a separate action. Re-issue the illustrated part list with the new sealant and grommet call-out. Agree an access sequence with the cabin office so the lining panel removal is written once and referenced by both the sealing task and the drain grommet installation.

similarity_seeds: standing moisture and sealant blistering at a longitudinal skin joint
drainage of the fuselage bilge area on an early-build aircraft

tasks.title: Collect the repair history at the joint land on the early fleet
Search structural repair practices covering the same zones
Identify the manual content carrying the sealant call-out

expected_findings.rationale: The general oversize hole and plug repair practice is already embodied at the joint land on a large part of the early-build fleet. The proposed sealant bead runs straight across those plugs and no qualification exists for a bead laid over a plugged and re-protected land.
expected_findings.resolution: Released with a condition: the plug population is recorded from the repair file before embodiment and the bead is terminated clear of it. Qualification handed to the materials laboratory as a separate action.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure lists the joint fastener and both skin items and carries the sealant call-out in its note block. The new standard changes the sealant and adds a drain grommet that the figure has no item number for.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issue the figure with the new call-out and a new item for the grommet, timed with the production cut-in rather than with the bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The joint cannot be reached without taking the cargo compartment lining panels out, and the removal task is written for panel replacement rather than for structural access. Two different sequences would otherwise be published for the same work.
expected_findings.resolution: Reference the existing removal task from the sealing procedure instead of writing a second access sequence.

expected_findings.rationale: The aft compartment harness runs along the same sill as the new drain path. The drain outlet position was moved forty millimetres inboard during the analysis so that water leaving the joint cannot track onto the harness support.
expected_findings.resolution: Drain outlet position agreed with the wiring owner and reflected on the installation drawing; no change to the wiring sheet.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned on the zone seed because the sill frame insert repair is worked from the same access, but it is a frame web repair above the joint land and shares no fastener, no sealant and no drain feature with the standard.

type_data.conclusion: Released with one condition on the plug population at the joint land; the qualification of a sealant bead over a plugged land was carried out separately.
